messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGING: Elevated 502/504 and KV miss storm for tenant MedLogix on dedicated eu-central-1 pool. Pager fired 2026-03-15T14:12:01Z.

mario (oncall): ack. I'm on it. quick status: is this everywhere in the pool or limited to a subset of hosts?

tara (eng-runtime): looks concentrated to two racks (rack-17a) serving medlogix partitions; prefix hit-rate per-tenant collapsed from 88% -> 5% and node memory pressure spiked. lots of small ephemeral prefixes: /medlogix/session/* and /medlogix/tmp/*.

sam (sre): grabbing host-level metrics and recent GC/OOM logs. can someone pull per-tenant kv quota and ring assignment?

tara (eng-runtime): pulling control plane:
```
$ curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" https://controlplane.internal/v1/tenants/medlogix/meta
# returned: pool: dedicated-eu-central-1, kv_quota: 10GB, assigned_rings: [r17a,r17b], ttl_default_s: 60
```

nina (support): Customer-facing: MedLogix reported degraded API responses and "empty summary" errors. They're escalating to their engineering lead. Leo, can you ping them?

leo (customer-success): pinged. asking for any recent integration changes. so far they say a canary release yesterday included a logging+session bake but nothing obvious.

mario (oncall): immediate mitigations we can do: 1) enable per-tenant isolation mode to switch to tenant-local caches (tenant-shield), 2) apply temporary backpressure at ingress for high-cardinality prefixes, 3) cold-warm differentiation: bump TTL for stable prefixes. which is fastest?

tara (eng-runtime): tenant-shield toggle is fastest. it changes kernel policy on the serving nodes to allocate private cache slabs for the tenant (segmented LRU). flip command:
```
# enable tenant-shield for medlogix
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" \
  -d '{"tenant":"medlogix","isolation":"segmented_lru"}' \
  https://controlplane.internal/v1/tenants/medlogix/isolation
```

sam (sre): while that's rolling, we should also apply an ingress rule to limit per-prefix QPS for obvious tmp prefixes to slow the churn. can do via edge rate-limiter.

mario (oncall): tara, can you roll tenant-shield now? i'll put ingress limits in place.

tara (eng-runtime): running toggle. starting canary on rack-17a (2 nodes), 20s observation window.

incident-bot: change-event: tenant isolation change started (id: iso-22b7)

sam (sre): seeing immediate drop in cross-tenant eviction spikes on rack-17a; hotkey counts for medlogix move into their own slabs. overall pool hit-rate improves from 6% -> 42% on canary nodes. 5xx rate on those nodes drops.

nina (support): MedLogix says some endpoints are responsive again but still seeing errors on batch endpoints.

leo (customer-success): relayed. they want to know whether this is a permanent change and if it affects cost.

tara (eng-runtime): tenant-shield does reduce shared cache efficiency slightly (10-15% overhead per isolated tenant) but prevents pollution. we can roll back once they fix client behavior.

sam (sre): ingress QPS limiter for prefixes matching /medlogix/tmp/* set to 20r/s per prefix. command applied at edge.

mario (oncall): next step: snapshot hot keys and blacklist evict the noisy tmp prefixes from tenant slab so we don't keep useless entries. tara, can you export top-k prefixes?

tara (eng-runtime): exporting top prefixes now: `/medlogix/session/active`, `/medlogix/patient/meta`, `/medlogix/tmp/` (high-cardinality range), `/medlogix/logbatch/`

incident-bot: utility: hotkeys snapshot saved to seclog://hotkeys/medlogix-1860054321.json

tara (eng-runtime): evicting tmp/* ranges and applying TTL bump for stable prefixes:
```
# evict and ttl updates
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" \
  -d '{"tenant":"medlogix","evict_prefix":"/medlogix/tmp/","overrides":[{"prefix":"/medlogix/session/active","ttl_s":1800}] }' \
  https://controlplane.internal/v1/tenants/medlogix/cache-ops
```

sam (sre): after eviction and isolation roll, pool-wide medlogix hit-rate up to 61%, rack-17a cleared memory pressure. 5xxs primarily gone; remaining 504s from long-running batch jobs that do large scans.

nina (support): told MedLogix the fixes and asked for confirmation on whether their recent canary included any high-cardinality session keys. awaiting reply.

leo (customer-success): they confirmed a telemetry change accidentally started writing per-interaction session keys with unique IDs under /medlogix/tmp/ — they will patch.

mario (oncall): handing to Sam for monitoring and postmortem ownership. summary for next oncall: root cause: client-side high-cardinality ephemeral keys + low default TTL + shared LRU => cache pollution and memory pressure -> downstream timeouts. mitigations done: tenant-shield (segmented LRU), ingress per-prefix QPS limiter, eviction of tmp prefixes, TTL bump for stable prefixes, hotkey snapshot exported.
sam (sre): ack. I'll keep a 2-hour watch, collect profiles, and start postmortem draft. owners: ENG-RUNTIME (tara) to recommend permanent isolation knobs and cost model; SRE (sam) to produce timeline and runbook; CS (leo/nina) to send customer-facing incident note and action items.

incident-bot: incident update: mitigations applied; monitoring for 120m. incident status: mitigated (customer impact reduced).

mario (oncall): quick note: consider adding auto-detect for sudden per-tenant high-cardinality prefix growth and automated temporary isolation. Tara, add to design backlog.

tara (eng-runtime): added ticket INF-4721: auto-detect + throttle + auto-isolate. I'll include simulation plan.

nina (support): sending customer note now with timeline and ask for the patched release.

sam (sre): final check: 5xx < 0.2%, latency within SLOs. leaving monitoring and will update if any regressions.

incident-bot: incident closed for oncall Mario; monitoring continues. :white_check_mark:
